title: Conditional authorization export record (synthetic, v1)

required_fields.decision: enum: PASS | DEGRADE | VETO  (semantic states; names illustrative, binding decisions belong to assignees)
required_fields.obligations: array of typed obligations; explicit field, MUST be present even when empty
required_fields.obligation_object: {id, type, description, due (before|during|after action), fulfilled: true|false|null (null = not yet evaluable), evidence_digest}
required_fields.diagnostics: array, distinct codes: E_UNSUPPORTED_PROFILE | E_INVALID_CHAIN_LINK | E_EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE | E_POLICY_OMITTED_ARGS | E_POLICY_OMITTED_FIELD (added v1.1.0: a required field was omitted entirely by policy, e.g. obligations absent rather than empty)
required_fields.record_digest: sha256 over canonical serialization of all fields above

distinguishing_rule: A reader outside the runtime can distinguish authorization-without-obligations from authorization-with-obligations IFF the obligations field is explicitly present in the exported record (empty array vs non-empty). If the field is omitted by policy or the profile is unsupported, the correct output is a diagnostic code, not a PASS. Note the three states are not interchangeable: obligations: [] asserts 'no obligations apply'; obligations: null (case4) marks an unanswerable question under an unsupported profile; an absent key (case5) is an unrecorded policy omission — the record alone cannot distinguish it from a lossy export.
